Dr. Ben Hinds
Psychiatry Registrar
Marourba Hospital
Lakes Road
Marourba

Commented [mg1]: Maroubra

07/03/2011

Dear Doctor,

Re: Mr Yuxiang Meng, aged 21 years

I’m writing to refer Mr. Meng, a Chinese student chef who presented today with an acute manic
episode. Your urgent attention would be appreciated.

Today Mr. Meng presented with an elevated mood and unusual behavior. On examination, he was
found delusional, pressured in speech, and loose in association. He refused medication, thus he
was referred to RNSH ED, Mental Health Assessment was scheduled and the local Mental Health
team was notified.

Initially, on 02/03/2011, he was admitted complaining of pharyngitis; however, he seemed
tangential and in an elevated mood. No signs of organic syndromes were found, consequently, lab
tests were ordered, to confirm the clinical findings; and, a referral to the Mental Health team was
arranged who gave him and diazepam was given under their supervision.

On the next day, the tests ruled out any organic pathology; additionally, the Mental Health team
confirmed the diagnosis of non-organic mania and ruled out harm to self or others. Nevertheless,
he was still tangential, therefore, he was prescribed quetiapine. Today his uncle mentioned that he
might not have been taking the medication.

In light of the above, I would be grateful if you would manage his condition as you see appropriate.
Kindly note that he speaks very basic English and might need a referral to a Chinese speaking
psychiatrist in the future.

Yours faithfully,
Doctor
